A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Superposition Yields Robust Neural Scaling by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization in v3.

before.justification: V1 reports original toy-model training experiments, representation-geometry analyses, and evaluations of four LLM families on four text datasets, including supplementary results.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and LLM evaluations and reports revised geometric diagnostics in Section 3.2 and Appendix D.6.

M1.justification: Both use the same tied-weight ReLU autoencoder, synthetic input generation, reconstruction objective, and modified AdamW weight-decay/growth update. V3's correction concerning optimal biases changes the theoretical analysis, not the documented training procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain synthetic feature reconstruction with power-law, exponential, and linear frequency distributions, plus language-model evaluation and token-frequency analysis on Wikitext-103, Pile-10k, C4, and BookCorpus. No new task, domain, or input scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: The weak/strong-superposition comparisons and random-unit-vector references remain. OPT, Qwen2.5, GPT-2, and Pythia remain the analyzed LLM families. Newly cited research is not introduced as an evaluated competing algorithm; the changed overlap statistics concern evaluation rather than comparator membership.

E3.justification: The geometric diagnostics change: v1 Figure 15 evaluates absolute-overlap variance across negative weight decays, whereas v3 Figure 5c evaluates squared-overlap variance normalized by its random-vector expectation at gamma = -0.55. V3 Figure 17 averages overlaps across all vectors at gamma = -1, replacing the weak-feature-only summary across negative decays. The main training and LLM evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D.6 revises the evidence testing ETF-like geometry through the squared-overlap variance diagnostic and an all-vector overlap-scaling analysis, replacing the earlier weak-vector-only plot. Activation-density sensitivity and the width-50–150 robustness experiment already appear in v1 and are retained.

E5.justification: V3 Appendix D.1 newly explains that Figure 1 error bars are standard deviations over 100 evaluation batches. Captions for Figures 4, 5, 15, and 18 identify standard errors. These clarify uncertainty reporting without establishing additional training runs; both versions still report one LLM evaluation per model–dataset pair.

E6.justification: V3 newly reports normalized squared-overlap variances and all-vector mean overlaps that decrease approximately as 1/m, replacing v1's absolute-variance and weak-vector overlap summaries. These involve different statistics or subsets, not same-setting performance gains. The headline LLM exponent 0.91 ± 0.04 and inferred Chinchilla exponent 0.88 ± 0.06 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (4) corrects ignored-feature loss from the second moment to the variance, incorporating optimal biases and explaining when the squared-probability term is negligible. Section 3.2 adds the Beta distribution and moments of random-unit-vector squared overlaps. The Welch bound, principal scaling predictions, and Appendix A cross-entropy expansion are retained.

C1.justification: The main claims about distribution-sensitive weak superposition, robust inverse-width scaling under strong superposition, and agreement with LLM observations remain. V3's abstract additionally frames the contribution as explaining when scaling can improve or break down, extending the claimed implications.

C2.justification: V3 shifts the strong-superposition explanation toward generic isotropic geometry, with ETF structure explaining error correction and skewed-frequency behavior treated more cautiously. Its Discussion replaces v1's impending-inefficiency and above-70B depth-scaling speculation with conditional predictions about exponent improvement and vocabulary-scale breakdown. It also adds coefficient-versus-exponent qualifications and interpretability/safety tradeoffs.

D1.justification: V3 Appendix B.2 explicitly lists the six model widths, and Appendix D.6 supplies the parameters of the illustrative norm-distribution example: m = 15, alpha = 1, gamma = -0.78. These refine documentation; the existing hardware, training recipes, processing instructions, script names, and repository location remain.

R1.justification: V3 adds references on feature learning, computation in superposition, compressed sensing, and interpretability. Section 4 also distinguishes the intrinsic feature-frequency exponent from the model/data-dependent kernel-spectrum exponent. These are targeted additions within the existing research positioning; many other reference edits are bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: V3 extensively rewrites the abstract and substantial parts of Methods, Results, and Discussion. It introduces an explicit research question, concept summaries, and three highlighted results; divides Results into weak-superposition, strong-superposition, and LLM subsections; and reorganizes appendix material. Acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist are added.

P2.justification: The visual narrative is substantially redesigned through boxed summaries and revised main figures. The weak-superposition loss plot changes axes and grouping, and the geometry figure reorganizes panels and incorporates the variance diagnostic. V1 Figures 4 and 7 move to appendix Figures 9 and 14 in v3, while many other plots are reused and repacked.

improvement.justification: The corrected weak-loss derivation, clearer distinction between generic geometry and ETF structure, and added all-vector overlap check improve the accuracy and support of the explanation. Defined error bars and reorganized results also make the evidence easier to assess. The improvement is limited: the toy-model-to-LLM connection remains heuristic, and the new predictions about scaling improvement and breakdown remain conditional rather than experimentally established.
